articles.title: Football Daily - MNC:Leeds dreaming of Europe and when's the right time to start a young player? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Mark Chapman is joined by Conor Coady, Chris Sutton and Rory Smith.
articles.body:
Radio 5 Live , · 23 Nov 2026 , · 60 mins

articles.title: Copa do Mundo Feminina: Fifa anuncia sedes de 2031 e 2035 | G1
articles.standfirst: Foram candidaturas únicas e conjuntas, com 4 países-sede cada uma
articles.summary: A Copa do Mundo Feminina terá sedes nos EUA, México, Costa Rica e Jamaica em 2031, e no Reino Unido em 2035, com novo formato expandido para 48 seleções nacionais.
articles.body:
A Fifa confirmou nesta segunda-feira (23) as sedes das Copas Femininas de 2031 e 2035.

Foram candidaturas únicas e conjuntas, com quatro países-sede cada uma. A confirmação veio em um congresso extraordinário da Fifa, que contou, de forma virtual, com a participação das associações-membro da entidade. Primeiro, Gianni Infantino, presidente da Fifa, anunciou que a Copa do Mundo de 2031 vai ser nos Estados Unidos , México , Costa Rica e Jamaica.

Cindy Parlow, presidente da Federação de Futebol dos Estados Unidos, disse que eles vão usar essa oportunidade histórica para acelerar o crescimento do futebol feminino no mundo. Serão 20 estádios distribuídos em 20 cidades – 14 nos Estados Unidos, quatro no México, uma na Costa Rica e uma na Jamaica.

Em 2035, o Mundial vai voltar à Europa. A última edição no continente havia sido na França, em 2019. Desta vez, Inglaterra , Escócia, País de Gales e Irlanda do Norte , os quatro países que formam o Reino Unido , foram os escolhidos para receber a competição.

Conheça as sedes das Copas Femininas de 2031 e 2035 — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

A presidente da Associação de Futebol da Inglaterra, Debbie Hewitt, afirmou que, juntos, eles vão inspirar as próximas gerações e reunir fãs de todos os cantos do mundo. Serão 19 estádios em 15 cidades. A maioria delas na Inglaterra, com 11, e duas na Escócia, uma no País de Gales e uma na Irlanda do Norte.

Diferentemente da Copa do Mundo Feminina de 2027, que vai acontecer no Brasil e vai contar com a presença de 32 seleções, as edições de 2031 e 2035 vão ser maiores e terão o mesmo formato da Copa do Mundo Masculina de 2026: 48 seleções serão divididas em 12 grupos com quatro equipes. Trinta e duas avançam à fase de mata-mata. Serão 104 jogos no total.

Infantino destacou que se mais meninas puderem jogar perto de casa e se mais mulheres puderem treinar e liderar, então as Copas terão feito algo que vai além do apito final.

articles.title: Women's World Cup: UK announced as 2035 hosts as Costa Rica, Jamaica, Mexico and USA host in 2031
articles.summary: The tournament will be the first football World Cup to be held in the UK since 1966; 48 teams will be involved, with matches played at19 venues across England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland
articles.body:
The bid was unopposed after FIFA declared it the sole valid bid in April 2025 and ratified it at an Extraordinary FIFA Congress meeting on Monday.

It will be the first time the nation has hosted a football World Cup since the men's World Cup in 1966.

The 2035 edition will be the second tournament featuring 48 nations, following 2031, which will be hosted by Costa Rica, Jamaica, Mexico and the United States, whose bid - which also ran unopposed - was also confirmed to be successful.

The dates for the tournament are yet to be confirmed.

It will take place across 19 stadiums across 15 cities, with one additional host city and three additional stadiums for future consideration.

Presenting the bid at the FIFA meeting, Sky Sports News presenter - and non-executive FA director - Jess Creighton said: "Welcome to your Women's World Cup 2035. A tournament where we want every team, every fan and every nation to feel at home.

"Across the UK, football has always been about bringing people together - and that's why, in 2035, we'll welcome it the way football always has: by helping everyone feel at home.

"Our ambition is to deliver the most-watched FIFA Women's World Cup ever.

"We're predicting in 2035, there will be more than 3.5bn viewers, and over 4.5m tickets sold."

English Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt addressed the Congress after the bid's success had been confirmed.

"Thank you for your trust and confidence in awarding us the FIFA Women's World Cup 2035," Hewitt said.

"We're deeply honoured by your support and grateful for the opportunity to host the pinnacle of women's football on behalf of the global football family.

"As we said throughout our bid, we want this to be your FIFA Women's World Cup, a World Cup for everyone.

"Together, we will celebrate the power of women's football, inspire the next generation, and unite fans from every corner of the world. We look forward to welcoming you to the United Kingdom in 2035 and just as importantly, to working closely with you all in the years ahead to deliver an exceptional FIFA Women's World Cup that the entire football community can be proud of."

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: "The world is coming to the United Kingdom. In 2035 the biggest tournament in women's sport will be played in cities across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, bringing visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country.

"Our players have inspired a generation of girls. In 2035 that generation will watch the best in the world play on their doorstep - and some of them will be on the pitch. But the impact of this World Cup will go much further. It will reach into communities across the country, bring more people into the game and leave a legacy that lasts long after the final whistle."

images.caption: Image: The 2035 Women's World Cup will take place in the UK

articles.title: David Raya injury update: Arsenal keeper's shoulder injury not too serious says boss Mikel Arteta
articles.summary: Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya will miss Tuesday's Champions League game against Borussia Dortmund but his shoulder injury will not require an operation.
articles.body:
Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya's shoulder injury "doesn't look too serious", but he will miss Tuesday's Champions League against Borussia Dortmund, says Mikel Arteta.

Raya was helped off the pitch in the 70th minute of Arsenal's 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Saturday.

He hurt his left shoulder while claiming a cross and making contact with Newcastle forward William Osula.

"We need some more tests [on Tuesday] but it is quite encouraging," said Gunners boss Arteta.

"He is not fit [to face Dortmund] but it doesn't look too serious."

Arteta said that while the incident looked pretty innocuous the pain his keeper was in made him fear it was a serious injury.

"With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action we were all quite worried but it seems to be better than what we expected," said Arteta.

"When you look at the action it doesn't seem to be much but the extent of the pain that he had and how he was struggling, it was quite worrying.

"We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had in that moment.

"The first tests that we have done have shown something that is much more encouraging. He does not need to have surgery which was the worry as that would rule him out for months so let's see."

Raya set to have scan on injury - how much would Arsenal miss him?

Arsenal face Borussia Dortmund, Manchester City , Brentford , Tottenham Hotspur and Real Madrid in their next tranche of matches.

And Raya is huge part of the way that Arsenal play because of his ability with the ball at his feet.

When asked if losing Raya for a long period of time would be the biggest blow to his team, Arteta said: "We have seen what David brings to the team but as well that is why we are very protective with Kepa [Arrizabalaga] and Illan [Meslier].

"Everybody needs to be ready because these things unfortunately happen and now we need to show everyone how well we are protected and the good keepers that we have in Kepa and Illan."

images.caption: Image caption, David Raya is Arsenal's first choice goalkeeper and has won the Golden Glove for the last three seasons in the Premier League.

articles.title: Women's World Cup 20235: Northern Ireland 'positive' over stadium upgrades required to host World Cup
articles.summary: The Irish Football Association's director of women's football Angela Platt says they are "still working through" plans with the Northern Ireland government to ensure there is funding available to make the necessary upgrades to Windsor Park in time for the 2035 World Cup.
articles.body:
The Irish Football Association's director of women's football Angela Platt said the organisation is "still working through" plans with the Northern Ireland government to ensure there is funding available to make the necessary upgrades to Windsor Park in time for the 2035 World Cup.

It was confirmed on Monday that Northern Ireland, England, Scotland and Wales, the only bidders for the tournament in nine years' time, had been ratified as co-hosts.

Of the 19 venues proposed by the 'All Together' bid, Belfast's Windsor Park is the sole stadium in Northern Ireland, but would require an additional 5,000 seats to its current capacity of 18,500 as well as changes to the pitch and floodlights.

"We're obviously working with our government partners who've committed their support to help us do that, and we'll continue our endeavours to make sure that we work towards that," Platt told BBC NI's Stephen Watson.

"We know that the Northern Ireland Executive has given a commitment to back us and do whatever they can to support us in our endeavours to make sure we're ready for that hosting of the Women's World Cup in 2035.

"We have a few years to make sure we work through that."

Northern Ireland was involved in a similar bid to host games at Euro 2028, but plans for fixtures in Belfast at that tournament fell through when the government said it would not provide funding to redevelop Casement Park in the required timescale.

Platt said that "was in the past" and that the organisation were focused on the work required to avoid any repeat.

"We're still working towards making sure that it does happen and we're positive. We know that the work is there to make sure that it happens," she added.

"It's obviously disappointing when something that people work so hard to put together doesn't come to fruition, but certainly that's in the past for us.

"From our perspective, working for women's football, this is a great opportunity for Northern Ireland to get behind this and actually make sure that we do everything we can to host our Women's World Cup games here."

UK to host 2035 Women's World Cup, Fifa confirms

Plans to increase Windsor Park capacity to 23,750

'It can only have benefits for Northern Ireland'

There is no guarantee that, even as co-hosts, there would an automatic qualification spot for Northern Ireland.

The side last qualified for a major tournament at Euro 2022 and Platt believes bringing the World Cup to the country has the potential to "inspire a new generation".

"I think it can have a huge impact. We've always been blessed that we have had our women's team involved in the Women's Euros in 2022, and through my role, I get to visit other nations hosting tournaments such as this," she said.

"I was in Sydney for the Women's World Cup (2023) and obviously saw the impact hosting a tournament like that had in New Zealand and Australia, and likewise for the Euros in England and Switzerland recently.

"That impact is significant. It's the growth of the game, it's the engagement, it's the legacy. So much positivity can come out of hosting major tournaments and we're excited to play our part in this and it can only have benefits for Northern Ireland in general."

articles.title: USA, Mexico Among Locations for 2031 FIFA Women's World Cup, Latest on Potential Host Cities
articles.summary: FIFA announced Monday the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will jointly host the 2031 Women's World Cup.
articles.body:
FIFA announced Monday the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will jointly host the 2031 Women's World Cup.

"We are incredibly honored and excited to welcome the world to the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica for the 2031 FIFA Women's World Cup," U.S. Soccer president Cindy Parlow Cone said . "This is a historic moment for our four countries, but the opportunity is much bigger than any one of us. Together with FIFA, we want to deliver the biggest and most impactful Women's World Cup in history and use its success to accelerate the growth of women's soccer around the world.

"Our ambition is to create a tournament that not only inspires millions of players, but helps give them the opportunities to play, grow and pursue their dreams."

The host cities are still to be determined. The U.S. listed 14 prospective sites in the official bid book, which included Atlanta, Houston, Seattle, Arlington, Texas, and East Rutherford, New Jersey.

FIFA's decision was effectively a fait accompli. The North American joint bid was the only official one on the table. The same thing was true for the 2035 World Cup, which will be shared between England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.

Having four host countries is a reflection of the expansion of the Women's World Cup. Starting in 2031, the tournament will grow from 32 to 48 teams, matching the number of competitors in the men's tournament.

This will be the third time the United States has helped to stage the event, having held the distinction in 1999 and 2003. Canada is the only other North American country to have had hosting duties.

The United States goes into basically every Women's World Cup with the aim of winning the whole thing, though a round-of-16 exit at the hands of Sweden in 2023 showed how the U.S. women's national team is no longer the dominant force in the sport.

Having a World Cup on home soil is going to set the expectations even higher in another five years.

articles.title: Dundee: Steven Pressley reflects on Hearts thrashing
articles.summary: Steven Pressley says he felt embarrassed by Dundee's 8-0 "humiliation" by Hearts and that there is a "fragility" in his squad.
articles.body:
Head coach Steven Pressley has admitted that "at times, I've wanted to crawl under a rock and hide" after Dundee's 8-0 "humiliation" by Heart of Midlothian.

Two days after the Dens Park debacle, Pressley is still adamant he must shoulder the blame - despite winger Alan Forrest earlier saying the "freak" result was down to the players.

Pressley said after the game he was concerned a poor result was imminent and admits he had sensed some complacency within the squad.

"Our strength has been built on cohesion, unity and aggressiveness," said the head coach, who said he was embarrassed by the result but that at difficult times he "seems to find strength from somewhere".

"I think Saturday highlighted exactly what I've been saying - if we get lazy on the hard yards, we're a very vulnerable team.

"We have to be, as I've been consistent all along, at our absolute best to get results.

"I've sensed a little bit of subconscious complacency and my job is to ensure that doesn't seep into their performance."

Pressley on wanting to 'crawl under a rock', complacency & 'direct' culture

Hearts bounce back from 'rocky patch' with Dens 'demolition'

Pressley believes "there is a little bit of fragility in the squad - certain players of huge talent but a little bit fragile mentally" and must now lift them to face a Hibernian side on Tuesday who are hurting from a 4-0 home defeat by Dundee United.

"It's been a difficult 24, 48 hours," he admitted. "There's been a lot of hurt, a lot of embarrassment.

"At times, I've wanted to crawl under a rock and hide on the back of such a disappointing result.

"But I will say this, you know I suffer a lot from vulnerability at times, but for some reason during difficult moments, I seem to find strength from somewhere. I do and I've had to show strength.

"But we had a good meeting on Sunday. We chatted a lot about the various aspects and hopefully we can start responding to the disappointment."

Pressley said he knew pre-match "that we're nowhere near as good as people tell us we are" and he had previously tried "various things" to guard against a poor performance.

"I've been trying to introduce a couple of things within their training, within our debriefs on games," he revealed.

"But obviously what I have tried to do hasn't had the right effect and, when you get a performance like Saturday, which lacked that intensity, lacked those hard yards, that's on me because I have to make sure that they're ready for that."

It was the first time the former Scotland centre-half has suffered such a heavy defeat as a player or manager.

"There's been some really disappointing days, disappointing results, but of course when you're the head coach and it's my responsibility then this ranks as one of the worst," he added.

"I've been in football for nearly 36 years and you think what have I not experienced and then this comes along. It's the great thing about football - it just keeps testing you.

"We have to use days like this as a reminder to ourselves - as a reset moment. I just hope we can bring some pride back to the football club with the right type of performance against Hibs."

images.caption: Image caption, Steven Pressley says there is a "fragility" in the Dundee squad
Image caption, Steven Pressley was left shocked by Saturday's 8-0 home defeat

articles.title: FIFA picks US-led bid as 2031 Women’s World Cup host and UK project for 2035 edition
articles.summary: The United States is going to be a soccer World Cup host again in 2031 and England will do so for the first time since 1966.
articles.body: The United States is going to be a soccer World Cup host again in 2031 and England will do so for the first time since 1966. FIFA on Monday confirmed the U.S. will lead a four-nation, regional co-hosting of the 2031 Women’s World Cup — with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica — and a UK project led by England was ratified for the 2035 edition. The winning candidates and FIFA president Gianni Infantino promised commercially successful tournaments — the first editions with 48 teams and 104 games — and to reinvest all that money in women’s soccer. “This will be the largest women’s sporting event in history,” the U.S. Soccer Federation president, Cindy Parlow Cone, told FIFA members in a pre-vote presentation at the governing body’s headquarters in Zurich. “Which means we have to deliver.” FIFA wanted these heavyweights of women’s soccer to face no opposition without rival bids and so lead hosting the first expanded tournaments. That will bring parity with the men’s World Cup which expanded to 48 teams this year in the U.S., Canada and Mexico. The 2027 Women’s World Cup will have 32 teams in Brazil. The U.S.-led 2031 project across the CONCACAF regional soccer body bid offers FIFA a choice of stadiums in 20 cities: 14 in the U.S., four in Mexico plus San José in Costa Rica and Kingston, Jamaica. The United Kingdom bid joins England with Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales that offers a choice from 19 venues, including Wembley Stadium in London. The pair of four-nation co-hosting bids had a clear run in the past 20 months and were approved Monday by acclamation in an online meeting of FIFA’s 211 member federations. The U.S. previously hosted the Women’s World Cup alone in 1999 and 2003. The national team’s tournament win in 1999 was the second of its four titles. England never hosted a Women’s World Cup which started with the 1991 tournament in China, won by the U.S. In the men’s World Cup, England hosted for the only time in 1966 and won its only title. Northern Ireland gets its chance for major tournament hosting role The UK bid includes Northern Ireland which has plans for Windsor Park in Belfast for a renovated 23,000-capacity stadium. That is big enough for a Women’s World Cup but not for the men’s European Championship. Euro 2028 is being hosted by England, Scotland, Wales and Ireland, which has the 50,000-seat national soccer and rugby stadium in Dublin. A pair of double World Cup hosting awards with no rival bids For the second time in less than two years, FIFA is confirming a double award of World Cup hosts without rival bids that gives clarity for the decade ahead. In December 2024, FIFA member federations were asked to rubber-stamp the unprecedented six-nation, three-continent bid for the men’s World Cup in 2030 from Spain, Portugal, Morocco, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay. That cleared the way for FIFA to award also the 2034 World Cup to Saudi Arabia in a fast-track process that seemed designed to exclude other candidates.

articles.title: Rangers vs Aberdeen: Derek McInnes ready for different Dons challenge under Mario Frick, live on Sky
articles.summary: Rangers can move to within a point of Scottish Premiership leaders Celtic with a win on Tuesday night, Mario Frick led Aberdeen to a much-needed league win in his first game in charge at Kilmarnock; watch Rangers vs Aberdeen, live on Sky Sports from 7.15pm
articles.body:
The Ibrox side are at home to Aberdeen on Tuesday night, live on Sky Sports, which is their game in hand over Scottish Premiership leaders Celtic.

A win would move them to within a point of their Old Firm rivals and give them the chance to move back to the top of the table on Saturday, for 24 hours at least.

Rangers have eight games between now and the end of December, including a League Cup final, as they bid to win their first piece of silverware for three years.

"You don't want to make too many changes when you're winning games because you'll be kicking yourself," McInnes told Sky Sports News .

"That's a fine balance. I think that it's important to keep these boys interested, to keep them fit for when they do go in as well, because training is one thing, but everybody wants to play and be available to play and start the weekend.

"Tomorrow night, we might look to freshen it up in one or two areas and then head to the game on Saturday for something similar."

Rangers are unbeaten in their last 11 Premiership games, a run that started with a 1-0 win away to Aberdeen in late August.

"We've not conceded too many goals in that run and we've been quite settled as a team, given to maybe two or three players coming in and out, and I think that's helped us.

"But I do think, getting into this one, we're in a good place, but we all know how quickly that can change. You've just got to be confident with our work, but not complacent.

"Hopefully we'll get our reward for a big performance tomorrow. I actually think we'll really need to play well tomorrow."

McInnes also led his side to a League Cup semi-final win against the Dons last month, but he is expecting a different challenge now Mario Frick is in charge.

"It's the third time we've played Aberdeen this season and it'll be the third different shape we come up against," the former Dons manager added.

"There are added challenges here, but we just need to really make sure we're as good as we can be and hopefully we can get the three points.

"With a new manager, the players have got a lot to prove to him and they'll be able to build on their win on the weekend.

"But for us, it's important that we concentrate on our levels and if we can get our levels, it'll give us a chance."

Frick delivered a much-needed win at Kilmarnock on his Aberdeen debut to lift them up to eighth in the table.

But, the Liechtensteiner is under no illusion about the different challenge that awaits them in Govan.

"It's another opponent with more quality than Kilmarnock, so we have to improve our defence, that's for sure," Frick told Sky Sports News .

"Their quality is also in transitions when they win the ball, they are very, very dangerous. So we have to improve.

"I'm pretty confident that we can show our game.

"We want to try to press them also, not only to wait them, and then without transitions I think it can be dangerous."

articles.title: Hibernian: Marink Reedijk rejects Easter Road jinx talk
articles.summary: Hibernian manager Marink Reedijk rejects suggestions Easter Road is jinxed after going seven months without a home win in the Premiership.
articles.body:
Manager Marink Reedijk has rejected suggestions Easter Road is jinxed despite Hibernian being without a home win in the Scottish Premiership for more than seven months.

Hibs have lost nine of their last 10 home league games, with the 3-0 victory against Kilmarnock on 4 April under former manager David Gray the last success in the Premiership in front of their own fans.

Reedijk - in charge for seven matches, three of which have been at home - believes a focus on "brilliant basics" can end that dismal run on Tuesday night against Dundee, who conceded eight at home to Heart of Midlothian at the weekend.

"We need to be ourselves, need to show what we're capable of, show what we've worked at, who we are," said the Dutchman.

"On Saturday we didn't represent ourselves in that way. Therefore if we start to do these things well in a consistent manner, I don't see that anything is jinxed whatsoever. It's up to us."

The wretched sequence stretches back to the end of last season, when Hearts, Celtic and Motherwell won after the Premiership split and continued this season with the Steelmen and their Edinburgh rivals triumphing again at Easter Road.

Victories for Kilmarnock, Falkirk, Celtic and the mauling at the hands of Dundee United have been punctuated only by a draw against similarly out-of-form Aberdeen.

I've wanted to crawl under a rock and hide' - Pressley

Dundee Utd eight unbeaten after stylish four-goal thrashing of Hibs

"The basics we've been doing well in the other matches, we didn't do them on Saturday. That was for me, I wouldn't say a shock but it was surprising," Reedijk added.

"Saturday didn't represent who we are and didn't represent the week's training we had. It is important you are consistent in the things you do.

"I keep repeating the word consistency and the basic things that make us good: being intense, being brave in trying to go forward, being on the front foot, being proactive and sticking together.

"For me the key is to do things consistently and to be happy to do the brilliant basics over and over and over again."

The Dens Park club might be ideal opponents for Hibs to be facing - the last Dundee manager to win in Leith was Ivano Bonetti more than a quarter of a century ago.

articles.title: Arteta desactiva la alarma con Raya: "No tendrá que pasar por quirófano"
articles.standfirst: Confirmó que no estará mañana contra el Dortmund... pero que la lesión "no parece grave"
articles.summary: Confirmó que no estará mañana contra el Dortmund... pero que la lesión "no parece grave"
articles.body: La lesión sufrida por parte de David Raya en St. James' Park contra el Newcastle dejó helada a la parroquia 'gunner'. Mikel Arteta, sin embargo, se ha encargado de desactivar la alarma en la previa del partido contra el Borussia Dortmund en Champions. "No parece muy grave", señaló el técnico del Arsenal. Unas palabras alentadoras teniendo en cuenta las notables señas de dolor que transmitió en el hombro un David Raya que no pudo continuar el partido contra los 'magpies'. De hecho, se ha confirmado que no tendrá que someterse a una cirugía. "Aún tenemos que hacer más pruebas, pero tiene buena pinta", se aventuró a confesar Arteta. Confirmó, eso sí, que "no podrá jugar contra el Borussia Dortmund". "Con el dolor que mostró tras el golpe estábamos preocupados, pero parece que va a ser mejor de lo esperado. No va a tener que pasar por quirófano, lo que le hubiera dejado varios meses fuera". De hecho, el entorno del jugador ha confirmado a MARCA que, en función de la evolución, podría llegar a jugar contra el Manchester City el próximo fin de semana. De este modo, su compatriota Kepa Arrizabalaga volverá a enfundarse los guantes para defender la portería del Arsenal. Será la segunda vez que el canterano del Athletic Club, quien sigue siendo el portero más caro de todos los tiempos, arranque de inicio en lo que marcha de temporada. Viene con cierto ritmo después de jugar con la selección vasca durante el parón... además de tener que disputar los últimos 20' ante el Newcastle.

articles.title: Euro 2028: When is the qualifying draw and how does it work?
articles.summary: Our Ask Me Anything team tell you all you need to know about the Euro 2028 qualifying draw.
articles.body:
The Euro 2028 qualifying draw will take place on Sunday, 6 December at 17:00 GMT at the International Convention Centre in Belfast.

It will form the twelve groups that make up the qualifying group stage; six containing four teams and six containing five teams.

All 54 Uefa member associations will enter qualifying at the group stage.

Despite hosting the 2028 tournament, the UK home nations and the Republic of Ireland must also participate in qualifying rounds.

The 54 teams have been divided into five pots based on their interim overall ranking in the 2026-27 Nations League following the conclusion of the league phase.

Pots one to four contain 12 teams, and pot five contains six teams.

The teams will then be drawn into the 12 qualifying groups, with the four host teams, as well as Northern Ireland, drawn into different groups.

The four winners of the Nations League quarter-finals must be drawn into a group containing four teams.

Twenty teams, made up of 12 group winners and eight best runners-up, will advance directly to the tournament proper. The eight highest-ranking runners-up will be based on the overall qualifying rankings.

If host nations fail to win or are runners-up in their group, there will be two spaces in the tournament proper reserved for the best-ranked nations at the end of the group stage, regardless of how many other host nation teams have qualified.

As a result, the final number of teams in the tournament proper will be between 20 and 22 nations, depending on the performance of the host nations.

How can teams qualify for Euro 2028 via the Nations League?

There are also qualifying routes available through the 2026-27 Nations League.

Nations League final rankings will also determine the seeding of nations for Euro 2028 qualification.

You can read more on how the process works here .

Pot One: England , Portugal, France, Germany, Spain, Belgium, Netherlands, Norway, Greece, Italy, Denmark, Croatia

Pot Two: Wales , Serbia, Turkey, Czech Republic, Switzerland, Sweden, Austria, Northern Ireland , Slovenia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Hungary, Republic of Ireland

Pot Three: Ukraine, Scotland , Kosovo, Poland, Israel, Romania, Georgia, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Albania, Iceland, Slovakia

Pot Four: Estonia, Belarus, Faroe Islands, Cyprus, Finland, Moldova, Armenia, Bulgaria, Kazakhstan, Luxembourg, Latvia, San Marino

Pot Five: Malta, Azerbaijan, Lithuania, Andorra, Gibraltar, Liechtenstein

When are the Euro 2028 qualifying fixtures?

Matchday seven: 30 September-2 October 2027

Where will the host nations play if they qualify?

If the host nations and/or Northern Ireland qualify for the tournament proper, they will have dedicated slots at stadiums:

England (Group B): Etihad Stadium (one match), Wembley Stadium (two matches)

Northern Ireland (Group D): Tottenham Hotspur Stadium (one match), Villa Park (one match), Wembley Stadium (one match)

Republic of Ireland (Group E): Dublin Arena (three matches)

Scotland (Group F): Hampden Park (three matches)

Wales (Group A): National Stadium of Wales (three matches)

If the hosts and/or Northern Ireland qualify via the play-offs, they will still be assigned to their designated group, but will not play all their group matches in the locations mentioned above.

articles.title: How does Mauricio Pochettino halt Man Utd's desperate slide
articles.summary: How does Mauricio Pochettino halt Manchester United's desperate slide towards the foot of the Premier League
articles.body:
Manchester United's Premier League trip to Anfield was described by some as a free hit for new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

The theory was expectations for United were so low as they travelled to Liverpool that a positive outcome would be a huge bonus, and anything else was expected.

But Pochettino did not look like a man without pressure after 15 minutes of what turned into a 4-0 defeat.

By that point, his side were already 2-0 behind and down to 10 men. Liverpool's fans were gleefully singing about the Argentine being "sacked in the morning", even though he was only a sixth of the way through his first game in charge.

A day later, United supporters began filtering through Manchester Airport on their way to Lisbon for a Champions League match that marks the next stop in what has turned into a desperate campaign.

The prevailing mood was one of resigned acceptance punctuated by dark humour around what a season in the Championship might look like, and whether Manchester City might be there with them.

United's England midfielder Kobbie Mainoo summed the situation up when he spoke to MUTV after the final whistle at Anfield.

"We're at the lowest we've ever been and no-one's coming to save us," said the 21-year-old.

"There are no helping hands coming, so we've got to work together, lean on each other, keep working and hopefully it will come good.

Tough tests before the transfer window opens

United are giving little away about their plans for the January transfer window.

For now, it is being stressed, Pochettino's priority is to get the most from the players currently at his disposal.

However, there was sympathy with former boss Michael Carrick's belief he had been let down in the summer window and there was a plan to address that.

That situation remains. A striker is thought to be Pochettino's priority given United's only recognised number nine, Benjamin Sesko, is out at least until January with a shin issue that has bothered him since March.

United have a long-standing issue at left-back. First choice Luke Shaw missed his eighth successive game on Sunday and the only other orthodox left-back in senior ranks is England Under-20 international Harry Amass, who didn't even make the bench at Anfield.

However, Pochettino worked with Shaw at the start of his career at Southampton and feels the 31-year-old can be a positive influence on his group.

The reality though is United still have nine games to play before they can make any changes to their squad.

Among those fixtures are home games against Coventry, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland.

Newly promoted Coventry are four points ahead of United, who are second from bottom. Forest and Sunderland are in the two positions immediately above the Old Trafford club.

A trip to Crystal Palace - the one side below United, and the other Premier League club to replace their coach during the international break - looms on 13 December.

After Wednesday's encounter with Sporting, Pochettino's side have one Champions League game before the end of the year - against RB Leipzig on 8 December.

Any solutions to be found to the current mess over the next five weeks have to come from within. If they don't, light-hearted discussions about a first relegation since 1973-74 under Tommy Docherty start to get serious.

"They have got enough in that squad to get themselves out of the bottom three," Ashley Young - a Premier League winner with United - told Match of the Day.

"They have not been showing that, but Pochettino has only just come in. He is going to want to get his team set up in a way that they are hard to beat. Right now, they do not look like they are hard to beat.

"It doesn't look like there is that togetherness. He has got to find a way to get that out of them. I am sure he will be able to do that when he has been longer in the job."

Pochettino shut down a question about United's terrible recent defensive record when he spoke to the media immediately after the game at Anfield.

"Tell me only about the circumstance today," he said. "I wasn't [here] in the past."

That is true - and may also have been a useful diversion exercise in avoiding a dissection of a defensive unit he is still getting to know.

However, Pochettino knows United have kept one clean sheet all season - against Azerbaijani champions Sabah FK in September. He will also know United have now conceded 19 goals in their past six games.

Pochettino's big decision at Liverpool was to pick Matthijs de Ligt in the centre of a three-man defence ahead of Harry Maguire.

"He played in the Champions League you know, before the internationals," said the former Tottenham, PSG and Chelsea boss.

In the 4-1 loss at Como on 21 October, De Ligt made his first appearance in 11 months following major back problems that eventually required surgery, largely because Leny Yoro was suspended and Lisandro Martinez was injured. He then played for two minutes against Roma on 3 November, when he was thrown on as then manager Carrick searched desperately for a winner.

Most goals can be broken down into a number of mistakes that compound to make an eventual negative outcome.

Team positioning has been mentioned as a reason De Ligt found himself exposed under a high ball at Anfield. However, his failure to deal with it presented Alexander Isak with a clear run at goal and prompted Yoro to make the tackle that led to his controversial dismissal, which Pochettino felt shaped the 82 minutes that followed.

But United have been conceding bad goals all season. Numerous players have been culpable.

There is a limit to what Pochettino can do in the time available. However, he wants to maximise what he can do.

Whereas Carrick tended to let his starting players have a day off after matches, the new regime has decided a warm-down session at Carrington is the better option.

And defensive organisation was surely one of the key points his coaching team had on their list of things to work on when the players began preparations to face Sporting on Wednesday.

Will January be the answer Man Utd need?

With £70m summer arrival Carlos Baleba injured for the second time since the start of pre-season, Pochettino must find a way to protect United's goal, which might require additional support in midfield.

The strengths of Mainoo and Youri Tielemans are with the ball. Either with three in the middle of defence or a third man in midfield, a way needs to be found to stop opposition attacks running straight at the defence.

In his recent interview with Sky Sports, United chief executive Omar Berrada said the club needed to be "disciplined" in the transfer market and avoid spending huge sums on players who would not necessarily make the squad better.

But the fact former Chelsea midfielder Andrey Santos went five games between Premier League starts under Carrick from the opening-day defeat at Hull - and was only introduced for the final three minutes at Anfield - suggests there are doubts over the Brazilian, who cost £48m in the summer.

Underneath that is the knowledge United borrowed from their revolving credit facility around all their major summer purchases and did the same again earlier this month when Pochettino was hired at a cost of just over £7.5m.

In public accounts released last week, United confirmed there was another £160m available in credit - but also they owe £417m in outstanding transfer fees, £236m of which is due within 12 months.

Neither before nor after the transfer window opens do any simple solutions to United's predicament present themselves.

Last season, fellow 'big-six' club Tottenham did not save themselves until the final day of the season.

Confidence remains high at Old Trafford the situation will not be quite so dire for them, but it could be a very bumpy ride.

articles.title: Emre Mor, tercer fichaje más caro del Celta, se retira por "problemas de salud mental" con 29 años
articles.standfirst: Firmó con el NEC Nimega el verano pasado
articles.summary: Firmó con el NEC Nimega el verano pasado
articles.body: Corría el verano de 2017 cuando el Celta desembolsó 13 millones de euros -tercer fichaje más caro de su historia- al Borussia Dortmund para firmar a Emre Mor. Era uno de los mayores talentos del momento... pero no llegó a cuajar en Vigo. Menos de una década después, con apenas 29 años, ha decidido retirarse por "problemas de salud mental". Desde que salió de Vigo, su carrera ha ido dando tumbos: Galatasaray, Olympiacos, Karagümrük, Fenerbahçe, Eyüspor... El pasado verano, se desligó del propio Fenerbahçe para firmar libre por un NEC Nimega que disputó previa de Champions y se clasificó para la Europa League. Marcó, de hecho, el gol contra Olympiacos que les dio acceso a la última ronda contra el Bodo/Glimt. Tras siete partidos disputados, Emre Mor sufrió una lesión inguinal que le ha mantenido fuera de los terrenos de juego desde mediados de septiembre. De forma completamente inesperada, sin embargo, ha tomado la decisión de retirarse. Al menos, de manera temporal hasta que sienta que su situación ha mejorado. "Desde pequeño, solo he tenido un sueño: convertirme en futbolista profesional. Poder vivir ese sueño lo ha significado todo para mí. Siempre he intentado darlo todo por el deporte que tanto amo", confesaba el talentoso jugador turco. "Sin embargo, últimamente he tenido algunos problemas de salud. He llegado a un punto en el que necesito escuchar a mi cuerpo, respetar mis límites y priorizar mi bienestar". "Por ese motivo, he tomado la difícil decisión de alejarme temporalmente del fútbol profesional y centrarme en mí mismo. Mi pasión por el fútbol nunca cambiará, y mantengo la esperanza en lo que el futuro me depara". Tenía dos años de contrato con el NEC Nimega. Pero, en este momento, ha decidido priorizarse. "Es un futbolista con mucho talento. El verano pasado, asumimos el reto juntos con la intención de ayudarnos mutuamente y darle la oportunidad de demostrar su talento. Lamentablemente, ha indicado que actualmente no puede rendir al nivel que desearía. Lo hablamos de buena fe y, finalmente, concluimos que esta es la mejor opción para ambas partes. La salud de una persona siempre es lo primero. Le deseamos a Emre todo lo mejor en esta situación y en el futuro", explicó Carlos Aalbers, director deportivo del NEC Nimega.

articles.title: Football’s first billionaire Cristiano Ronaldo invests nearly €20M in giant Portuguese bottled water plant expected to produce up to 600 million litres annually for global markets
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has invested nearly €20 million in a state-of-the-art bottled water plant in Portugal, set to produce 600 million liters annually for global markets. Discover how this venture aligns with his impressive business portfolio.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo has spent much of his career building a fortune through football, but his ambitions increasingly extend beyond the pitch. The Portugal forward is now backing a nearly €20 million bottled water plant in the country where his career began, with the facility expected to produce up to 600 million litres annually and send most of its output to international markets.Ronaldo backs €20 million water plant in northern PortugalThe new facility is being developed in Gostei, a small village in the municipality of Bragança in northeastern Portugal. It will draw water from a local spring and bottle it for distribution, with an investment of close to €20 million ($22.4 million).The project is being carried out through Maravilha Decimal, a company jointly owned by Ronaldo and Portuguese business group Grupo Outeirinho. According to Observador's report, based on reporting from the Portuguese news agency Lusa, the plant is expected to have an annual production capacity of between 500 million and 600 million litres, with most of the output intended for export markets.Francisco Ferreira, an executive at Grupo Outeirinho, has identified the mineral composition of the spring water as one of the project's principal selling points. The company intends to use those characteristics to distinguish the product as it pursues distribution in international markets.Construction is already under way, with completion targeted for the end of 2027 and commercial production expected to begin in early 2028. The facility will have separate bottling lines for glass and PET plastic containers, while developers expect it to create several dozen jobs in the region.The investment also builds on an existing partnership in the water industry. Ronaldo and his business partners launched Ursu9, a premium mineral water brand bottled in Spain, in June 2023. The Portuguese plant represents a further expansion of their interests in the sector, bringing production into Ronaldo's home country.From Ursu to hotels, clinics and media investmentsWater is only one part of the business portfolio Ronaldo has developed alongside his football career. His CR7 brand covers clothing, underwear, fragrances and footwear, while his hospitality interests include the Pestana CR7 hotel chain, established in partnership with Portugal's Pestana Group.The hotel portfolio has included properties in Lisbon, Madeira, Madrid, New York and Marrakech. Ronaldo is also a partner in Insparya, a chain of hair-transplant clinics, and holds a stake in Medialivre, the Portuguese media group that publishes Correio da Manhã and the sports newspaper Record.His first move into bottled water attracted considerable attention because of an earlier moment involving Coca-Cola. At a Euro 2020 press conference in June 2021, Ronaldo moved two Coca-Cola bottles away from his seat and held up a bottle of water instead. The gesture became widely discussed, although his Ursu venture followed two years later.The Bragança project gives him another foothold in an industry that can operate independently of his playing career, while also establishing a substantial manufacturing operation in Portugal.Ronaldo's fortune extends well beyond footballDespite his growing business interests, football remains the foundation of Ronaldo's wealth. He signed a contract extension with Saudi Arabian club Al-Nassr in June 2025, keeping him at the club until 2027, and has remained among the world's highest-paid athletes through his salary, bonuses and commercial agreements.Ronaldo was estimated to have earned around $275 million in 2025, according to figures cited in the business profile of his wealth. In October that year, he became football's first billionaire, with the Bloomberg Billionaires Index valuing his fortune at approximately $1.4 billion.At 41, Ronaldo is approaching the later stages of his playing career, but the investments in Portugal and elsewhere show how extensively he has diversified his interests. The new bottling plant is among his largest industrial ventures to date, with a scale of production that goes well beyond a personal brand or a small commercial partnership.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Iniesta, Silva, Cesc, Navas, Llorente... ¿Quiénes fueron los jugadores de la última goleada histórica de España?
articles.standfirst: Repasamos los jugadores que formaron parte del equipo que atesoraba la mayor goleada de las categorías inferiores de la Selección española hasta el día de hoy
articles.summary: Repasamos los jugadores que formaron parte del equipo que atesoraba la mayor goleada de las categorías inferiores de la Selección española hasta el día de hoy
articles.body: La Selección española sub-17 ha hecho historia en Doha. Aunque se ha quedado a un gol de igualar la mejor cifra goleadora en el Mundial de esta categoría, -16-0 de Marruecos ante Nueva Caledonia del año pasado-, los de David Cubillo han batido el récord propio de España en partidos de categorías inferiores. Con el 15-0 ante Fiyi, han superado por uno la cifra que el equipo dirigido por Iñaki Sáez estableció hace 21 años. El 8 de febrero de 2005, la Selección española sub-21 arrasó a San Marino y dejó en un escandaloso 14-0 la mayor goleada de su historia. Enmarcada en el grupo 7 del clasificatorio para el Europeo de esa categoría, España recibió en la cuarta jornada en El Ejido al combinado sanmarinense y no tuvo piedad de sus rivales. Aunque se trate de un resultado absurdamente abultado, haciendo un repaso de aquel equipo puede entenderse un poco mejor. El once inicial que dispuso Iñaki Sáez en el campo es bastante reconocible si atendemos a la trayectoria de sus carreras. Bajo palos estuvo Miguel Ángel Moyá, portero con una dilatada experiencia en el fútbol español en clubes como Mallorca, Valencia, Getafe, Atlético de Madrid o Real Sociedad. En la defensa, la compuesta por Melli, Dani Jarque, Murillo y Javier Garrido, el futbolista fallecido del Espanyol es el nombre más recordado. De hecho, el central dejó huella en ese encuentro, ya que anotó un 'hat-trick' en apenas 15 minutos. Pero sin duda, los jugadores con mayor calidad y empaque en sus posteriores carreras estaban del mediocampo para adelante. El doble pivote podía ser el del mejor Zaragoza, formado por Alberto Zapater y Gabi. A ambos lados de los organizadores del equipo, estaban Héctor Font, canterano del Villarreal, autor de un gol, y Andrés Iniesta, goleador apenas cinco años después del gol más importante de España en la final del Mundial de 2010 en Sudáfrica. En la punta de ataque, otros dos campeones del mundo. Un David Silva que en ese momento jugaba en el Eibar, secundando a un Fernando Llorente que empezaba a abrirse un hueco en el primer equipo del Athletic Club. En aquel partido, ambos jugadores anotarían un doblete. Y por si fuera poco, quedaba más pólvora en el banquillo. Los tres cambios de aquel día fueron Jesús Navas, que también marcó, y Cesc Fábregas, ambos protagonistas en el gol de Iniesta aquel 11 de julio de 2010, acompañados de un Jonathan Soriano al que le dio tiempo a anotar un 'póker' en los 45 minutos de la segunda parte que disputó. Otros jugadores que también estaban disponibles y que no disputaron ningún minuto fueron algunos como Asier Riesgo, Antonio Puerta o Santi Cazorla. Lo más curioso de aquella fase es que España también goleó (1-10) a San Marino en el partido de vuelta, pero eso no fue suficiente para clasificarse al Europeo del año siguiente tras quedar terceros por detrás de Bélgica y Serbia y Montenegro. En ese día histórico, por tanto, los goles para España fueron obra de: Jonathan Soriano (4 goles), Dani Jarque (3), Fernando Llorente y David Silva (2), y Jesús Navas y Héctor Font (1), sumado al que se metió Davide Vagnetti en propia puerta. Lo que está claro es que aquella goleada fue un presagio para jugadores que acabaron siendo estrellas mundiales. Una vez superada por la generación del 2009, sólo queda esperar y que el tiempo coloque en su lugar a grandes proyectos como Rafa Cruz, Guillermo Trujillano, Roberto Tomás, Holmes Júnior, Jorge Domínguez, Owen Emeka, Ebrima Tunkara o muchos otros... Por lo pronto, seguirán su propio camino para intentar conquistar el Mundial Sub-17.

articles.title: El emotivo homenaje sorpresa al Cholo en el entrenamiento
articles.standfirst: Plantilla, cuerpo técnico, Mateu Alemany y demás trabajadores del día a día rojiblanco le esperaron con una camiseta firmada por su récord de 345 victorias en la Liga
articles.summary: Plantilla, cuerpo técnico, Mateu Alemany y demás trabajadores del día a día rojiblanco le esperaron con una camiseta firmada por su récord de 345 victorias en la Liga
articles.body: Aunque por su mente no pasaba otra cosa que el Viking, el inicio del entrenamiento del Atlético en este lunes se vería alterado por la sorpresa con la que iba a encontrarse Simeone. Para cuando llegó al verde, todos los actores del día a día rojiblanco le esperaban para rendirle el merecido tributo por sus 345 victorias en la Liga que le convirtieron en el Coliseum en el entrenador más ganador de la historia. Con una camiseta con su nombre y la histórica cifra a la espalda y las firmas de todos ellos estampadas como recuerdo, allí le aguardaban del primero al último de sus acompañantes en cada jornada de trabajo: los jugadores, los integrantes de su cuerpo técnico, el conjunto de médicos, fisios y readaptadores, los utilleros, el delegado Pedro Pablo, el team manager Tomás Reñones y por supuesto un Mateu Alemany que tampoco quería faltar a la causa. La ocasión no era para menos. Un sentido homenaje de todos los que conforman la rutina diaria en El Cerro, evidenciándose la conexión, la cohesión y la unidad que existe entre la plantilla y los demás trabajadores, del buen ambiente que reina en el día a día y sobre todo de la fuerza del equipo, del vestuario y de los que lo rodean, salten o no al terreno de juego. Un momento de unión y reconocimiento al gran líder y artífice de la pasión y la energía con la que se afronta cada mañana en el Atlético. Eso sí, El Cholo no pudo evitar el tradicional pasillo de collejas con el que su familia deportiva quiso rendirle el merecido homenaje... y demostrarle que la llama se mantiene muy viva.

articles.title: Confianza total en Marruecos: el TAS le ratificará mañana como campeón de África
articles.standfirst: Mañana se conocerá la decisión definitiva y los 'Leones del Atlas' confían en conservar el título
articles.summary: Mañana se conocerá la decisión definitiva y los 'Leones del Atlas' confían en conservar el título
articles.body: La final de la Copa África entre Senegal y Marruecos disputada el pasado 18 de enero ha seguido jugándose en los despachos durante todos estos meses. Mañana, sin embargo, el TAS anunciará una resolución que, dictamine lo que dictamine, seguirá generando debate. Según fuentes consultadas por MARCA, la resolución seguirá siendo favorable a los 'Leones del Atlas'. O al menos ése es el pensamiento que se tiene entre los federativos marroquíes. Mediado el mes de marzo, la Confederación Africana de Fútbol le retiró el título a Senegal, que ganó el partido en el verde sobre el terreno de juego gracias a un gol de Pape Gueye en la prórroga, para otorgárselo a Marruecos. Todo, después de las denuncias emitidas por parte de la federación marroquí alegando que los 'Leones de la Teranga', previamente, habían abandonado el encuentro entendiendo que el arbitraje les estaba perjudicando. "Si, por cualquier motivo, un equipo se niega a jugar o abandona el terreno de juego antes del final reglamentario del partido sin la autorización del árbitro será considerado el perdedor y quedará eliminado de la competición en curso", establece el Artículo 82 de la CAN. El partido, automáticamente, se le dio como ganando a Marruecos por 0-3. Senegal, como no podía ser de otro modo, emitió alegaciones para conservar el título y apeló la decisión impuesta al TAS. "Es injusto, sin precedentes e inaceptable", llegó a pronunciar la federación. De hecho, se han encargado de ratificarle al mundo que se sienten los ganadores de la CAN paseando sus medallas. Durante todos estos meses, el Tribunal Superior de Arbitraje Deportivo ha estudiado el caso. Pero, apoyándose en el marco legal del torneo, Marruecos mantendrá la corona de campeón. Brahim Díaz, de este modo, podrá seguir presumiendo de ser el único futbolista del Real Madrid que levantó algún título la temporada pasada.

articles.title: Chris Hogg interview: Northampton boss out to change culture after relegation as takeover involving Pato offers hope
articles.summary: In this exclusive interview with Sky Sports, Northampton Town manager Chris Hogg discusses the challenge of turning their fortunes around after relegation last season. A consortium involving Pato offers hope but changing the culture remains the priority...
articles.body:
The former Brazil forward brings a bit of glamour to the Cobblers and their Shoe Army will welcome that. But for Chris Hogg, in his first job as a manager, the day-to-day challenge of turning this struggling football club around continues - and it is hard work.

While the long-term prospects have improved off the pitch, Northampton's revival was always likely to be difficult after such a miserable relegation. It was a dismal season at Sixfields. The campaign completely unravelled, ending with 12 consecutive defeats.

Dropping down a division was never going to make the problems go away. "Relegated teams have found it difficult in League Two. I was very aware of that," Hogg tells Sky Sports . It needed an overhaul, a radical shift in mentality. "Boys with experience of winning."

Hogg has experienced that in his own career, as a player with Hibernian and as assistant manager to Liam Manning at MK Dons, Oxford United, Bristol City and Norwich City. But this is his first taste of life as a number one and it has been some introduction for him.

Visiting him at the club's training ground, Hogg reveals that there were 150 messages on his phone when he was appointed in May and another 300 or so the next day. "Eighty per cent from unknown numbers." Many were agents. Welcome to the life of a manager.

Asked what the biggest change is, he says: "The volume of decisions. At other clubs, a decision might be half made before it comes to you. Here, it comes directly your way. It could be coaching, media, sports science, medical. The chain of command stops here."

Hogg took steps to prepare for the challenge of being a first-time manager in the lower leagues, making the strategic decision to add knowledge around him. He turned to long-time contact Chris Doig, an experienced assistant and a former player for Northampton.

"He has been promoted with this club, has been promoted at this level as an assistant before too. That all went into the mix. He knows what the job looks like for an assistant. We are different personalities and we challenge each other but we are very aligned."

At Northampton, everyone has to muck in and help wherever they can. And that is the way they like it. "Everyone is kind of at full tilt and doing about three different jobs. But it is great. It is a really tight-knit club and you have to embrace that," says Hogg, laughing.

"The goalkeeper coach brought his drill in one day."

Hogg has fashioned a small space into a makeshift office at the club's training ground. "A place to have the difficult conversations or just go through clips with players." The club were an analyst down during pre-season so much of that work was done himself.

He admits it has been "eye-opening in a good way" but he prefers to work this way. "It can become a stretch but if you can get that sweet spot where everyone is accountable that is better than having three people for a job and things falling between the cracks."

Hogg himself was among those making the calls to arrange some time at St George's Park in pre-season. "It was a change of scenery and a chance to show them what good looks like. It helped to accelerate relationships. It is about giving the boys no excuses."

He has worked hard to improve the working environment for the players. Overgrown bushes have been cut back to create more space. Exercise bikes have been moved to an outdoor area to declutter the medical area. The ice baths are being used again.

There is a breakfast club now and, with no kitchen, they are using an outside supplier to improve the quality of the food offering for the players. Hogg is not so keen on the idea of marginal gains, he regards these as fundamentals in changing the culture at the club.

"It might sound really simple but what food are we giving the boys? Are we getting the nutrition and the hydration right? Sometimes that is not there in clubs," Hogg explains. "We are just making sure we are on top of those basics. The rest is always nice to have."

He adds: "Everyone in football chases the one per cent, the flashy new thing, the trends. We cannot do everything, we are a football club that has to live within our means. So I have gone hard on nailing the basics. We have to be brilliant at the basics."

On the pitch, that has meant tightening up. The Cobblers are the lowest scorers in League Two but they also have a better defensive record than any team in the top six. Partly, it reflects the attempt to build a younger team and take a longer-term approach.

The signing of Matty Warhurst broke the mould for a club in Northampton's position. Young acquisitions from top teams are usually loan moves. But they paid a transfer fee to Manchester City to bring in Warhurst, who only turned 20 years old in September.

"There are certain things that you need in terms of physicality, pace and experience but one thing I look at is the ceiling of the player. I would rather take someone like Matty who has loads of room to get better than someone at the end of their career," Hogg explains.

"We put a lot into the recruitment process and we did our homework as well. Normally, there is always something when you speak to five or six people about a player but with him the reference all came back the same. He has the work ethic that we are looking for.

"The exciting thing is that it is a permanent deal. It was a coup for us really to get him out of Man City. Sometimes you have to think about how you can do the best for the club in the mid-to-long term. He is here for three years. If he does well, it will benefit everyone."

This challenge of whether to focus on the short term or the long term is a recurring theme for those in Hogg's position and there are those who would argue that a first-time manager would be wiser to focus purely on results in order to protect his own position.

But, in a way, the club's takeover makes it more straightforward. Whatever happens in the future, Hogg wants to play his part in building for it. "I will always make decisions for the long term, for the club, knowing that I am not going to be here forever."

He explains: "Everything that I am doing is to make this football club better, to build it in the right way. If I am here long term then that is great, but I want to know that I am making decisions so that no matter what happens the club will be in a better place."

Against Rochdale on Saturday, they came from behind to win a game for the first time in over a year. Perhaps those little cultural changes are starting to reap rewards. It is a long road ahead. But there are chinks of light at Northampton Town after too many dark days.

articles.title: La presunta fuga de un león pone en riesgo el Galatasaray-Aston Villa
articles.standfirst: "Se ha localizado la zona donde se encuentra el león y se están haciendo todos los esfuerzos posibles para capturarlo con vida", declaró la Oficina del Gobernador de Estambul
articles.summary: "Se ha localizado la zona donde se encuentra el león y se están haciendo todos los esfuerzos posibles para capturarlo con vida", declaró la Oficina del Gobernador de Estambul
articles.body: Un suceso insólito ha alterado la tranquilidad de Estambul en la víspera del encuentro de Liga de Campeones entre el Galatasaray y el Aston Villa. Un león ha sido avistado en una zona boscosa situada a unos 16 kilómetros del estadio RAMS Park, escenario del partido que ambos equipos disputarán este martes. Según informa el diario británico Daily Mail, las autoridades turcas pusieron en marcha un amplio dispositivo para localizar al animal y tratar de capturarlo antes de que pudiera poner en peligro a los residentes de la zona. El primer avistamiento se produjo en el distrito de Sariyer, al norte de la parte europea de la ciudad. Según las informaciones locales, agentes de una comisaría de la zona de Zekeriyakoy detectaron a través de las cámaras de vigilancia, alrededor de las 21.00 horas, la presencia de lo que describieron como "un animal parecido a un león". La búsqueda movilizó a cerca de 70 personas, entre policías y efectivos de emergencias y protección de la fauna, además de siete drones desplegados para tratar de localizar al felino. Las autoridades establecieron importantes medidas de seguridad en los alrededores de la zona boscosa en la que se sospecha que permanece el animal, así como en las villas próximas. El acceso al área quedó restringido y los residentes recibieron advertencias para extremar las precauciones. La propia Oficina del Gobernador de Estambul confirmó que los equipos de búsqueda habían conseguido delimitar el lugar en el que se encontraba el león. "Se ha localizado la zona donde se encuentra el león y se están haciendo todos los esfuerzos posibles para capturarlo con vida", señaló en un comunicado oficial. La noticia también ha provocado algunas escenas surrealistas en Turquía. La conexión futbolística del incidente no ha pasado desapercibida, ya que al Galatasaray se le conoce popularmente como los Leones y el escudo del Aston Villa también incorpora la figura de este animal. Incluso un medio de comunicación llegó a entrevistar a una persona disfrazada de león y vestida con una camiseta del conjunto turco para comentar lo sucedido, en una imagen que rápidamente llamó la atención. La anécdota llegó incluso al vestuario del Galatasaray. Abdulkerim Bardakci, defensa del equipo de Estambul, fue preguntado por la fuga del animal y respondió con humor ante la expectación generada en todo el país: "Quiero decir algo porque todo el país está hablando de esto ahora mismo. Solo hay un león que tengo en casa, y ese es mi hijo". Mientras tanto, los dispositivos de búsqueda continúan trabajando para capturar al felino.

articles.title: Big Ten Announces Title-Game Clinching Scenarios for UCLA, Oregon, Ohio State, More
articles.summary: The Big Ten released the championship game tie-breaking scenarios for Indiana, Iowa, Ohio State, Oregon, UCLA and USC on Monday.
articles.body:
The Big Ten released the championship game tie-breaking scenarios for Indiana, Iowa, Ohio State, Oregon, UCLA and USC on Monday.

The short version is this—if UCLA beats USC on Saturday they are in. If UCLA wins Oregon beats Washington on Saturday, they are both in. In any other scenario, things get complicated:

UCLA still completely controls its own fate, though Saturday's triple overtime loss against Michigan left them vulnerable to being left out of the Big Ten Championship Game entirely. Even with a loss, UCLA could get in, but it would take a more complicated scenario.

USC will be gunning for the Bruins with its own title game hopes still alive. The Trojans have been a bit erratic since a 4-0 start, but a victory over Ohio State in late October is a reminder that they are a real threat. The Trojans will still need a lot of help even if they knock off the Bruins, but their easiest path—Indiana, Iowa, Ohio State and Oregon all winning and Wisconsin losing—is plenty feasible.

Oregon, meanwhile, finds itself in good position for a title game berth as well given a four-game winning streak that has included victories over Northwestern, Ohio State, Michigan and Michigan State. They'll be favored at home against 7-4 Washington, though it's hardly a gimme.

Indiana's surprise loss against those Huskies on Saturday has left the Hoosiers needing a lot of help to get into the Big Ten Championship Game. A home game against 3-8 Purdue is more than manageable, but quite a lot is out of their hands in every scenario needed for them to get in.

Iowa's own four-game winning streak has them back in contention for a title game berth, and they'll be at home against 7-4 Nebraska. They are a long shot to reach the title game, however, needing one of several complicated scenarios to unfold.

All Ohio State needs to get in is a home win over Michigan alongside wins from Maryland, Rutgers and Wisconsin and losses from Indiana, Iowa, Oregon and USC. So yeah, probably not happening—those odds are minuscule.

But in Columbus, fans can still channel their inner Lloyd Christmas. Yes, we are in fact telling you there's a chance.

articles.title: "El responsable de la felicidad de un país"
articles.standfirst: El discurso de Juan Ignacio Gallardo
articles.summary: El discurso de Juan Ignacio Gallardo
articles.body: Pienso que el ser humano puede fingir todas las emociones, las personas pueden disfrazar todas las sensaciones, pueden aparentar todos los estados de ánimo… Todos menos la felicidad. La felicidad no se puede impostar, no se puede fingir, no se puede falsear. La felicidad es algo puro y extremo. Es la emoción suprema. La felicidad es un valor absoluto. La felicidad es lo que toda España sintió, a la misma vez, el pasado 19 de julio, cuando la selección se proclamó campeona del mundo de fútbol. Felicidad, que bonita palabra, qué bonito momento. Los artífices de ese episodio mágico e inolvidable fueron todos y cada uno de los que estuvieron en Estados Unidos: jugadores, fisios, directivos, analistas, personal de la federación, todo el staff técnico (¡qué maravilla teneros a todos hoy aquí!)… hasta el conductor del autocar seguro que puso su invisible granito de arena para que España levantara al cielo tan preciado y precioso trofeo. Pero el auténtico conductor de ese éxito coral y ejemplar, el causante de esa explosión de felicidad y alegría colectiva, el responsable de este éxito apabullante e imborrable fue nuestro gran protagonista, Luis de la Fuente Castillo. Él es quien ha cosido con maestría la segunda estrella a nuestra camiseta, con el mismo hilo de oro que ya utilizó Vicente del Bosque en Sudáfrica, y que también usó Jorge Vilda en Sidney con la selección femenina. Teneros a los tres aquí, a los campeones del mundo, a las tres personas que nos llevaron a la felicidad, a la gloria, es un lujo superlativo. Os doy las gracias en nombre de la audiencia de MARCA. Querido Luis, lo que pretendemos es devolverte, simbólicamente, toda esa alegría que has regalado a la afición. Has hecho y haces inmensamente feliz a la gente. Por eso queremos agradecerte y reconocerte como te mereces. Te hemos preparado este acto con un redoble de cariño y entusiasmo. El mismo que hemos percibido en nuestros millones de lectores, internautas, oyentes y followers, que convierten a MARCA en líder indiscutible y referencia mundial de la información deportiva. El mismo cariño y entusiasmo que hemos notado en todas las personas que abarrotan la sala, deseosas de acompañarte en este momento singular. Gracias a todos por realzar con vuestra presencia este acto. Nuestra galería de MARCA Leyendas, el más brillante y colosal ‘hall of fame’ del deporte universal, incomparable museo de la excelencia deportiva, abre su puerta grande para acoger a un nuevo miembro. Se trata del galardón número 100 que entregamos, desde que inauguramos tan excepcional relación con Michael Jordan, que fue el primero. Y me encanta que este número redondo, simbólico, excepcional, exclusivo y centenario, sea para De la Fuente. Sus méritos deportivos son indiscutibles: como jugador, con el Athletic -valor añadido- fue campeón de Liga dos veces, campeón de Copa y campeón de la Supercopa. Como entrenador ha sido Campeón del mundo, campeón de la Eurocopa, campeón de la Nations League, Campeón de la Eurocopa sub 21, campeón de la Eurocopa sub 19, campeón de los Juegos Mediterráneos, Medalla de plata olímpica, poseedor de un asombroso récord de partidos invicto… Pero si ese palmarés es dorado y resplandeciente, (como el bonito trofeo que le vamos a entregar) más brillantes si cabe son sus valores como persona. Y eso realza aún más su acreditación para recibir este galardón. Debo confesar que cuanta más cercanía tengo con el protagonista más rubor me produce ensalzarle. Y en este caso pintaré mi rostro con el rojo de la camiseta de España para intentar definirle y contaros acerca de él lo que ya sabéis los que le conocéis e imagináis los que no tenéis ese placer. Luis es un tipo sencillo, cordial, amigable. Buen conversador, simpático, divertido. También astuto, observador, reflexivo. Es firme, decidido, valiente, atrevido. De profundas convicciones, convincente y convencido. Autocrítico, inteligente, educado y comprometido. Pero no confundamos su bonhomía con debilidad o su cercanía con docilidad. Defendiendo sus posturas es batallador, luchando por sus ideas es combativo. De la Fuente es un tipo con talento. Un número uno universal. Un elegido. A ser campeón del mundo no llega cualquiera. A ser MARCA Leyenda, tampoco. Hoy tenemos el inmenso honor de entregarte esta distinción que sólo poseen los mejores. Es un trofeo, diseñado por el escultor José Onieva, que a mí me encanta. Tiene la forma de un ejemplar de MARCA doblado y está recubierto de un barniz dorado. Quiero que sepas que en el interior de ese periódico está el cariño infinito, eterno, de toda España. Y la admiración sincera, el aprecio verdadero, de los aficionados de todo el mundo. Enhorabuena y gracias por darnos tanta felicidad, Luis.
